target.title: feat(feishu): bot-to-bot conversation support with @mention handling
target.body:
## Summary

Makes Feishu bot-to-bot conversations actually work. Bot-authored messages already reach dispatch on `main` (nothing gates them out), so bots could already "talk" — but the experience was broken: replies frequently never reached the peer bot because the `@mention` was missing or used the wrong syntax for the payload, so the conversation silently died. This PR makes bot-to-bot replies reliable — correct, payload-aware `@mention` delivery on every visible path (text, chunked, card, streaming) — and adds opt-in (`allowBots`) plus loop-protection controls. (In a Feishu group a message only notifies the entities it explicitly `@mentions`, so a reply without the right `@` is silently never delivered.)

- Continue treating incoming bot messages like user messages (now gated by an `allowBots` opt-in) so the agent can take part in bot-to-bot threads.
- New `bot-name` resolution module backed by the bot batch API as a weak dependency: falls back to the `open_id` when the bot info scope is absent.
- Per-chat mention registry resolving display name → `open_id` for outbound use.
- Outbound mention handling: teach `<at user_id="...">` syntax in the system prompt, strip only the leading self-mention, preserve + dedup other mentions, escape `<`/`>` in display names.
- Guarantee bot-to-bot replies `@mention` the bot sender via a deterministic `ensureMention` backstop, applied **per outbound unit** (every text chunk and the streaming-card close) using the **syntax that matches the payload** — `<at user_id="...">` for text/post messages, `<at id=...>` for lark_md cards — so the peer bot is notified on every visible path. Replies are delivered inline, not in a topic thread.
- `allowBots` opt-in (default: accept, preserving current behavior) lets operators set `false` to ignore bots or `"mentions"` to accept only when `@mentioned`.
- Shared bot-pair loop guard: bot-authored turns are wired into core `botLoopProtection` (sliding window, on by default) plus a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes.
- Core owns the group reply-delivery mode; the feishu `@mention` hint stays delivery-mode-agnostic (no duplicate delivery-mode computation in the plugin).

Aligns with #71396 — main no longer auto-prepends mentions, so this does not reintroduce the third-party mention cascade: the `mentionTargets` block stays context-only and never tells the model to re-`@` listed users.

Scope: changes are under `extensions/feishu/**` plus the feishu docs page. The one non-plugin file is `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts`, regenerated (`pnpm config:channels:gen`) because the new `allowBots`/`botLoopProtection` config fields must appear in the aggregated bundled-plugin config metadata that the config-metadata check validates.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu` — green, including the new/updated `outbound-mention`, `reply-dispatcher`, `bot` (bot-authored handling), and `monitor` suites covering card vs text mention syntax, per-chunk mentions, `allowBots` gating, and loop-guard suppression.
- `pnpm config:channels:gen --check`, `tsgo`, and `oxlint` clean for the touched surface.
- Real-machine verification in a live Feishu group (see proof below).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a group bot-to-bot reply now `@mentions` the bot sender so the other bot actually receives it — across text messages, chunked replies, and lark_md cards; replies to a human still `@` the human; a silent turn stays `NO_REPLY`. With `allowBots: false` the bot ignores other bots' messages. Previously a bot replying to a bot could omit the `@` (or use the wrong card syntax) and the reply was silently never delivered.

Real environment tested: a live Feishu group containing two bots and one human participant; the agent ran as one bot and replied across multiple turns to the other bot and to the human, under both text and card render modes, and with `allowBots` toggled. (Identifiers below are redacted.)

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran `pnpm config:channels:gen`, rebuilt and restarted the gateway, then drove a multi-turn bot-to-bot exchange in the live group; captured the agent session trajectory and compared it against the messages actually delivered to the group; toggled `allowBots` and a tight `botLoopProtection` window to observe gating.

Evidence after fix:

- On turns where the sender was the other bot, the inbound prompt carried `[System: "<name>" (open_id: ou_<bot-sender-redacted>) is a bot and receives your reply only if you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]`, and the reply led with the bot sender's `<at>` — the peer bot received it.
- `ensureMention` backstop verified live: on a turn where the raw model output omitted the bot sender's `@`, the message actually delivered to the group still contained it — the dispatcher backfilled it.
- Card path verified live: a reply rendered as a lark_md card carried the card mention syntax (`<at id=...>`) and the peer bot received it (the text-form tag would not have notified inside a card).
- `allowBots` verified live: with `allowBots` disabled, the peer bot's messages no longer triggered a reply.

Copied live output from the session (open_ids and names redacted):

```text
# Inbound prompt to the agent — sender is the other bot:
[System: "<bot>" (open_id: ou_REDACTED) is a bot and receives your reply only if
 you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]

# Agent reply that turn, as delivered to the group — leads with the bot sender's <at>:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> 好，背景比较清晰，… (reply continues)

# A later turn whose raw model output dropped the bot-sender @ (it only @'d the
# human). The message ACTUALLY delivered to the group still carried it — the
# dispatcher's ensureMention backfilled the bot sender before sending:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> <at user_id="ou_REDACTED_HUMAN"><human></at> 面试结论：…
```

Observed result after fix: the other bot received and continued the conversation across turns under both text and card modes; no silent drop. `allowBots: false` cleanly suppressed bot-authored replies. Replies addressed exactly the intended target and stayed inline.

What was not tested: the `message_tool` visible-reply path does not receive the deterministic backstop by design (see Design notes); that is an intentional product decision, not an untested gap.

## Design notes

- **Per-payload mention syntax.** Feishu uses two `<at>` forms: `<at user_id="...">Name</at>` for text/post messages and `<at id=...></at>` for lark_md cards. The backstop emits the form matching each outbound unit and re-applies it per chunk and on streaming-card close, so a long or card-rendered bot-to-bot reply notifies the peer on every message.
- **The deterministic backstop is intentionally scoped to the `automatic` reply path, not `message_tool`.** `automatic` is an implicit reply where the agent does not directly control delivery, so the dispatcher guarantees the bot-sender `@`. The `message_tool` path (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`) is an explicit, flexible send where the agent deliberately authors the message, recipients, and mentions; the plugin respects what the agent wrote and does **not** auto-inject — forcing one would override an intentional, author-controlled send. Outbound mention normalization still runs on both paths, so any `@` the agent does write is resolved correctly.
- **Bot-pair loop protection.** Bot-authored messages already reached dispatch on `main` (no gate drops them), so the bot-pair possibility is not introduced here. This PR adds the safety: `allowBots` (default accept; `false`/`"mentions"` to restrict), a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes, and wiring of accepted bot-authored turns into core's shared `botLoopProtection` sliding-window guard (on by default). Tunable/disable-able via `channels.feishu.botLoopProtection`.

target.title: fix(sessions): make transcript migration rewrite atomic
target.body:
## Summary

- The one-time legacy linear→parent-linked transcript migration rewrote the whole conversation-history JSONL **in place** (`fs.writeFile` = `O_TRUNC` then write). A crash, power loss, or `ENOSPC` mid-write left the transcript empty or partially rewritten — **irreversible loss of user conversation history**.
- New path: the migration rewrite goes through a small `writeJsonlLinesAtomic` helper that writes an **fsync'd sibling temp file and atomically renames it** over the target. A failed rewrite now leaves the original transcript intact and is retryable. **Output bytes are unchanged.**
- The atomic rename changes the transcript's **inode**, which the embedded-attempt takeover fence's benign-rewrite classifier (`classifySessionFenceRewrite`, reached via `classifySessionFenceChange`) previously rejected because it required inode identity. The classifier is adjusted to be **content-based** (its per-line migration check is the real guard), and a **TOCTOU re-stat guard** binds the accepted baseline to the verified fingerprint so it cannot be swapped after benign classification.

Why this matters now: transcripts are a user-facing product artifact (conversation history). The migration fires once per legacy transcript on the next append after upgrade, so any real user upgrading across the linear→parent-linked format change is exposed to one-shot data loss on a mistimed crash/disk-full.

Intended outcome: a failed migration write leaves the existing transcript intact and retryable under the helper's temp+rename+fsync contract.

What success looks like: the migration is atomic (temp+rename+fsync), output is byte-identical, locking/append semantics are unchanged, and the takeover fence still rejects genuine takeovers.

What reviewers should focus on: the fence change in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.session-lock.ts` — see **Why the fence change is in scope** below.

### Why the fence change is in scope (please read before flagging it)

This is the non-obvious part of the PR, so it is called out explicitly:

- The atomic write replaces in-place truncate+write with **temp + rename**, which necessarily gives the rewritten transcript a **new inode**.
- `classifySessionFenceRewrite` exists specifically to recognize *this* linear→parent-linked migration as a benign in-process change while an embedded attempt is released for model I/O. It was written for the **in-place** rewrite and gated acceptance on `sameSessionFileIdentity` (same dev+ino).
- With the migration now atomic, that inode gate falsely flags the legitimate migration as `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (an existing test, *"allows delivery mirror appends that migrate legacy linear transcripts"*, fails without this change). So the fence change is **required by**, not incidental to, the atomicity fix.
- The **safety invariant for this benign-migration exception is content, not identity**: acceptance still requires every prior line to be exactly the parent-linked migration of the release-time snapshot (`lineMatchesLinearTranscriptMigration`) and every appended line to be a transcript-only OpenClaw assistant entry (`delivery-mirror` / `gateway-injected`). An inode-replacing rewrite whose content is not that exact benign shape is **still rejected as a takeover** (covered by a new test).
- The removed inode check only blocked the legitimate atomic temp+rename migration; for this recognizer, the narrow content matcher plus the re-stat baseline check is the meaningful defense.
- **TOCTOU:** because the classifier no longer pins identity, the transcript-only (no-merge) path in `assertSessionFileFence` now re-stats after classification and only adopts the new fence baseline if it still matches the fingerprint that was classified benign — otherwise it falls through to takeover. The merge path already enforces the analogous post-merge re-stat inside `mergePromptReleasedSessionChange`, so the guarantee holds on both paths. This closes the window where a rename-capable writer could show benign content to the check and swap different content into the trusted baseline.
- `classifySessionFenceAdvance` (the pure `O_APPEND` advance path, which is still genuinely in-place) **remains inode-gated** — only the rewrite classifier is relaxed.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes: N/A (no tracking issue)

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related: N/A; nearby prior art: an atomic temp+rename fix for `auth.json` landed previously (same pattern, different file). The in-flight transcript-writer refactor stack (scoped writer/seam PRs) touches `transcript-append.ts` and may require a trivial rebase; no semantic overlap.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No — proactive data-loss hardening.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** an interrupted one-time linear→parent-linked transcript migration could truncate/partially overwrite the user's conversation-history JSONL, losing it irreversibly.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw worktree at the PR head. A real legacy linear transcript was written to a real session directory on disk and migrated end-to-end through the production `appendSessionTranscriptMessage` (no mocked transcript writer), with a real `rename` failure (`ENOSPC`) injected at the atomic-replace boundary.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** a small harness drove the production migration against a real on-disk transcript and was run with `node --import tsx`; it created a legacy linear transcript, made the next `fs/promises.rename` throw `ENOSPC` once, called `appendSessionTranscriptMessage`, then inspected the on-disk file and retried. The committed deterministic version of the same scenario is `src/config/sessions/transcript-append.test.ts` (runnable by reviewers).
- **Evidence after fix:** live captured terminal output from the on-disk run (production code path, real injected disk-full failure):

  ```text
  transcript: /tmp/.../agents/main/sessions/repro.jsonl
  original bytes: 213, sha=f5d898dab594a9fb

  [1] migration write fails mid-rename (simulated disk-full):
      -> append rejected: ENOSPC: no space left on device, rename
      rejected:            true
      original preserved:  true (213 bytes, byte-for-byte equal)
      no temp left behind: true (dir entries: ["repro.jsonl"])

  [2] retry after the failure (rename restored):
      append succeeded:    true (lock was released after the failure)
      header version:      3 (bumped to current = 3)
      m1 now parent-linked: parentId=null (was linear, no parentId)
      appended entry:      type=message parentId="m2"
      total entries:       4

  RESULT:
    data-loss window closed = true
  ```

  Supplemental regression coverage (not the primary proof): the committed `src/config/sessions/transcript-append.test.ts` encodes the byte-identity / failure-injection / retry invariants, and `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` adds a test that an inode-replacing non-migration rewrite still raises `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.
- **Observed result after fix:** on the injected disk-full failure the original transcript stays byte-for-byte intact (213 → 213 bytes) with no partial write and no leftover temp sibling, and the call rejects; the retry then acquires the lock (proving it was released) and completes the migration to parent-linked form. Genuine takeovers are still detected.
- **What was not tested:** an actual hardware power-loss / kernel-level write tear (simulated via `rename`-boundary failure injection + `fsync` on temp and parent dir, not a real power cut); Windows rename-over-open-file behavior (POSIX-reasoned: old fd keeps old inode; a Windows sharing-violation surfaces as an operational error, not data loss); a deterministic race-injection test for the TOCTOU re-stat window (that guard is covered by code review, while hostile non-migration replacement is covered by a regression test).
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** crash/power-loss durability relies on `fsync` of the temp file and parent directory (best-effort per platform); deterministic proof uses failure injection at the rename boundary, which is the contract under test.
- **Before evidence (optional):** on the base commit the same injected-failure test against the in-place path leaves the transcript truncated/empty (the bug).

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `pnpm test src/config/sessions/transcript-append.test.ts` (migration byte-identity + failure-injection + retry)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.session-lock.test.ts` (migration-under-fence + new hostile-rewrite takeover test + all existing takeover tests)
- adjacent: `transcript-append-redact`, `transcript`, `transcript-stream`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` — all green

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- `transcript-append.test.ts` (new): (1) `writeJsonlLinesAtomic` is byte-identical and mode-identical (0o600) to `writeJsonlLines`; (2) rename-failure leaves the existing file intact with no temp sibling and rejects; (3) migration succeeds end-to-end producing valid parent-linked output; (4) original transcript intact after an injected migration-write failure; (5) retry after injected failure completes the migration (lock released).
- `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` (+1): an inode-replacing rewrite whose content is *not* a benign migration still raises `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Before: injecting a failure during the in-place migration write leaves the transcript empty/partial (data loss). After: the original is preserved and the write is retryable.

If no test was added, why not? N/A — failure-injection + invariant tests added.

Total: **105 (`attempt.session-lock`) + 5 (`transcript-append`) focused tests pass**; `tsgo` / `oxfmt` / `oxlint` green.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) — **No** for successful migrations (output bytes identical). The only behavior change is on failure: data is now preserved instead of lost.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) — **No** config/env. The transcript *migration* is made crash-safe; its successful output is unchanged.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) — **Yes (security-adjacent, please review):** the embedded-attempt takeover fence's benign-migration recognizer is relaxed from inode-identity to content-based, with a compensating TOCTOU re-stat guard. Takeover detection is otherwise unchanged; genuine takeovers still trip (tested).

What is the highest-risk area? The `classifySessionFenceRewrite` relaxation in `attempt.session-lock.ts`.

How is that risk mitigated? The per-line migration content check (unchanged) is the real guard; the in-place advance path stays inode-gated; a TOCTOU re-stat binds the accepted baseline to the verified fingerprint; a new test asserts hostile inode-replacing rewrites still raise takeover.

Privacy note: the sibling temp file holds transcript content during the rewrite; it is created in the same session directory with `0o600` mode and is removed on failure before returning. No new network or secrets surface.

### Intentionally out of scope (split follow-up)

- The sibling non-atomic whole-file rewrites in `agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.ts` and `agents/sessions/session-manager.ts` (incl. a `writeFileSync` variant) share the same torn-write shape but live in the SessionManager subsystem and overlap the in-flight SQLite session-store refactor. They are **deliberately not** in this PR and are named here as documented follow-up.
- No SQLite migration, no JSON-store reorder, no commitments changes, no ACP persist-ordering changes.
- **No `CHANGELOG.md` edit** (release-only per repo policy; release notes derive from this PR body).
- No ClawBench: this is a correctness / data-loss fix, not a performance change — proof is failure-injection + invariant tests, not latency/token measurement.

## Current review state

What is the next action? Maintainer review of the fence relaxation rationale + the atomic-write helper.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? Nothing from the author — tests/typecheck/lint green locally; CI pending on push.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? N/A (initial submission).

Rebase note (2026-06-20): rebased onto current `main` to resolve a `CONFLICTING` state, and the session-fence change was re-resolved against upstream's rewritten takeover flow (`classifySessionFenceChange` → `classifySessionFenceAdvance` / `classifySessionFenceRewrite`, plus `mergePromptReleasedSessionChange`). The atomic-write helper and migration call were unchanged; only the fence classifier's inode gate and the no-merge re-stat compensation were re-applied to the new structure, preserving the landed `sessionFenceCtimeDriftIsBenign` (Btrfs ctime), prompt-released merge, and write-lock-release-on-fence-read-throw behaviors. Post-rebase validation: the focused `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` (105) and `transcript-append.test.ts` (5) pass via the repo's `run-vitest` wrapper, and a fresh structured security review returned no actionable findings. No behavior change from the prior approved revision.

target.title: fix: trim trailing whitespace from final text-chunking chunk
target.body:
Fixes #64036. The final chunk emitted after the chunking loop was not trimmed with `trimEnd()`, unlike in-loop chunks. Also fix the same bug in Matrix's inline `chunkTextForOutbound` copy and update the guardrail test that hardcodes its source.

## Problem

`chunkTextByBreakResolver` in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts` was inconsistent: chunks emitted inside the loop were trimmed via `trimEnd()`, but the final chunk pushed after the loop preserved trailing whitespace. Matrix's inline `chunkTextForOutbound` in `extensions/matrix/runtime-api.ts` had the same bug.

## Changes

- **`src/shared/text-chunking.ts`**: Apply `trimEnd()` to the final `remaining` chunk and skip pushing when trimmed result is empty.
- **`extensions/matrix/runtime-api.ts`**: Same post-loop trim for the Matrix inline copy. Added under-limit early return (`limit <= 0 || text.length <= limit → [text]`) to match shared helper semantics and preserve the empty-string contract (`chunkTextForOutbound("", 10)` → `[""]`).
- **`src/plugins/contracts/plugin-sdk-runtime-api-guardrails.test.ts`**: Update hardcoded Matrix source string to match the fixed implementation.
- **`src/shared/text-chunking.test.ts`**: Add regression tests for final-chunk trailing whitespace and empty-after-trim cases.

## What previous PRs missed

| Gap | #64054 | #64079 | #72491 | #82421 | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shared `text-chunking.ts` final chunk trim | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Matrix `runtime-api.ts` inline copy | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Guardrail test update | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Preserve Matrix empty-string contract | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Preserve Matrix under-limit contract | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| No unnecessary Markdown IR scope creep | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

After-fix evidence from a real local setup (Node 22, Bun runtime, macOS ARM64):

**Shared `chunkTextByBreakResolver` — after-fix:**

```
chunkTextByBreakResolver("", 10, () => 5)
=> []

chunkTextByBreakResolver("  ! ", 2, w => w.lastIndexOf(" ") || w.length)
=> ["!"]

chunkTextByBreakResolver("a b ", 2, w => w.lastIndexOf(" ") || w.length)
=> ["a","b"]

chunkTextByBreakResolver("abc   def ", 6, w => w.lastIndexOf(" "))
=> ["abc","def"]

chunkTextByBreakResolver("   ", 2, w => w.lastIndexOf(" ") || w.length)
=> []

chunkTextByBreakResolver("alpha beta gamma", 10, w => w.lastIndexOf(" "))
=> ["alpha","beta gamma"]
```

**Matrix `chunkTextForOutbound` — after-fix:**

```
# Empty string — contract preserved from current main
chunkTextForOutbound("", 10)
=> [""]

# Under-limit trailing whitespace — preserved (text.length <= limit)
chunkTextForOutbound("hello ", 10)
=> ["hello "]

# Zero limit — preserved
chunkTextForOutbound("hello", 0)
=> ["hello"]

# Post-loop residual trailing whitespace — trimmed (the bug fix)
chunkTextForOutbound("alpha beta ", 8)
=> ["alpha","beta"]

# Normal multi-chunk
chunkTextForOutbound("hello world", 5)
=> ["hello","world"]

# Code-block-like content
chunkTextForOutbound("line1\nline2\nline3 ", 10)
=> ["line1","line2","line3"]
```

**Test suite:**

```
pnpm test src/shared/text-chunking.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/text-chunking.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts \
  src/plugins/contracts/plugin-sdk-runtime-api-guardrails.test.ts \
  extensions/matrix/src/outbound.test.ts

→ All 88 tests pass across 4 shards
```

target.title: fix(usage): exclude untimestamped records from daily ranges
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fixes ranged dashboard/session usage summaries so untimestamped cached transcript rows do not inflate selected-day totals or model usage.
- Keeps all-time cache summaries intact, but forces finite date ranges to derive from timestamped transcript rows only.

Why does this matter now?

- Issue #89709 reports that after v2026.5.28, Dashboard "今日模型调用" can show historical cumulative model usage for a selected day.

What is the intended outcome?

- A selected-day usage range only includes transcript usage rows with timestamps inside that range.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- No UI layout changes, provider pricing changes, Discord changes, memory-core changes, Mattermost changes, or MCP changes.

What does success look like?

- Ranged usage summaries exclude untimestamped historical records from total tokens, message counts, tool usage, model usage, daily breakdowns, and daily model usage.

What should reviewers focus on?

- The cache-derived session summary path in `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` and the deterministic regression fixture in `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #89709

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #87222

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

- ClawSweeper marked #89709 as source-repro, queueable-fix, and fix-shape-clear.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Selected-day Dashboard/session usage ranges no longer include untimestamped historical cached transcript records in model totals.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on branch `codex/89709-daily-usage-range`, using the actual `refreshCostUsageCache` and `loadSessionCostSummaryFromCache` runtime functions with a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `node --import tsx -` with a fixture containing an untimestamped historical `openai/glm-5` assistant usage row for 1000 tokens, an out-of-range dated `gpt-5.5` row for 10 tokens, and selected-day `gpt-5.5` usage for 20 tokens, then loaded the range `2026-02-05T00:00:00.000Z` through `2026-02-05T23:59:59.999Z` from the cache.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "cacheStatus": "fresh",
  "totalTokens": 20,
  "totalCost": 0.02,
  "messageCounts": {
    "total": 2,
    "user": 1,
    "assistant": 1,
    "toolCalls": 1,
    "toolResults": 0,
    "errors": 0
  },
  "modelUsage": [
    "openai/gpt-5.5:20"
  ],
  "dailyModelUsage": [
    "2026-02-05/openai/gpt-5.5:20"
  ],
  "dailyBreakdown": [
    {
      "date": "2026-02-05",
      "tokens": 20,
      "cost": 0.02
    }
  ]
}
```

- Observed result after fix: The ranged cache summary reports only the selected-day `gpt-5.5` usage; the untimestamped `glm-5` 1000-token historical record is absent from `totalTokens`, `messageCounts`, `modelUsage`, and `dailyModelUsage`.
- What was not tested: I did not run a browser Dashboard session against a reporter WSL2 profile or their real provider console data.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The reporter's actual local cache was not available, so the proof uses a deterministic temp state dir that exercises the same source-proven cache aggregation path.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): The prior source path only skipped out-of-range rows when `timestamp` existed, so untimestamped cached rows could still be added to ranged `totals` and `modelUsage`.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/usage.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/views/usage.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/usage-render-overview.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/usage.node.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:test-types`
- `git diff --check`

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Updated the cached session range regression to include an untimestamped historical model usage record and assert the selected-day summary only contains the timestamped selected-day model.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- The same cache-derived range path could include untimestamped records in aggregate totals and `modelUsage` because timestamp filtering only rejected entries with timestamps outside the range.

If no test was added, why not?

- A focused regression test was added.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Date-filtered usage totals and model usage now exclude untimestamped records.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

- Ranged usage summaries for legacy cached transcript rows without timestamps.

How is that risk mitigated?

- The change is limited to finite-range cache derivation. All-time summaries still include untimestamped entries, and regression coverage exercises the exact selected-day leak shape.

target.title: Fix Discord default account startup priority
target.body:
Fixes #77429

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Discord multi-account startup delay ordering previously followed the configured account id list directly, so a configured primary account such as `channels.discord.defaultAccount: "tech"` could be assigned a delayed startup slot when secondary account ids sorted before it.
- Real environment tested: Isolated OpenClaw PR-head worktree at `/private/tmp/openclaw-pr89744-proof`, commit `8deff209b4f468f2a9e704adfc63ec18de367444`, on macOS. The proof used the production Discord gateway startup function in `extensions/discord/src/channel.ts` with my real local multi-account Discord config and Infisical-injected real Discord bot token environment. A temporary in-memory config overlay set `channels.discord.defaultAccount = "tech"`; no token values were written to disk or included below.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```console
$ /Users/andy/.openclaw/workspace-tech/bin/infisical-env-run --paths /messaging -- \
    env PROOF_PR_HEAD=8deff209b4f468f2a9e704adfc63ec18de367444 \
    PROOF_ABORT_AFTER_MS=4500 \
    node --import tsx scripts/proof-discord-default-startup.ts tech
```

- Evidence after fix: Redacted live runtime log excerpt from the real Discord gateway startup path:


target.title: fix(ui): preserve autonomous tool failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When two autonomous agent turns are adjacent in Control UI history, a successful reply in the later turn could make a failed tool from the earlier turn render as Tool output instead of Tool error.

Fixes #97849. Supersedes #98888 after its contributor fork could not retain the reviewed rebase ancestry; contributor credit is preserved through co-authorship and the maintainer release-note batch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway chat-history projection preserves `sessions_send` input provenance while displaying those messages as assistant-side forwarded groups. The Control UI now treats only groups with `kind: inter_session` and `sourceTool: sessions_send` as autonomous-turn boundaries before annotating tool outcomes.

The implementation deliberately does not use `senderLabel` alone: ordinary relay-labeled assistant replies still count as replies to the current turn. Existing non-text assistant content behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Earlier autonomous tool failures remain visibly failed when a later autonomous turn recovers, while normal labeled assistant replies continue to mark their own tool turn as successful.

target.title: fix(gateway): allow macOS app platform version refresh without re-pairing
target.body:
## Summary

- macOS app enters infinite "Approve this Mac app to control OpenClaw" dialog loop after an OS update (e.g. macOS 26.5.0 → 26.5.1)
- Root cause: `resolvePinnedClientMetadata` treats any macOS platform version change as a `platformMismatch`, triggering a repair pairing request. The pending request has a 5-minute TTL, and when it expires before the user clicks Approve, the gateway returns "unknown requestId", causing the Mac app to send a new repair request — infinite loop.
- iOS and Android already had silent platform version refresh via `normalizeMobileAppPlatformPin` — this extends the same pattern to the macOS native app (`openclaw-macos` client ID) by recognizing `"macos X.Y.Z"` as the same platform family regardless of version number.
- Renames `normalizeMobileAppPlatformPin` → `normalizeNativeAppPlatformPin` and `isMobileAppPlatformVersionRefresh` → `isNativeAppPlatformVersionRefresh` to reflect the broader scope.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After a macOS system update (26.5.0 → 26.5.1), the OpenClaw Mac app enters an infinite loop of "Approve this Mac app to control OpenClaw" approval dialogs. Clicking Approve has no effect — the dialog immediately reappears because the gateway returns `INVALID_REQUEST: unknown requestId` (pending request TTL expired before approval arrived). The root cause is `resolvePinnedClientMetadata` treating any macOS platform version string change as `platformMismatch = true`, while iOS and Android already had silent version refresh.

**Real environment tested**: macOS 26.5.1 (updated from 26.5.0), OpenClaw gateway v2026.5.28 (node v24.15.0, npm `openclaw@2026.5.28`), OpenClaw.app Mac client (`openclaw-macos`, clientMode=node), local gateway at `127.0.0.1:18789`. The bug was discovered and diagnosed on this machine after the OS update broke the Mac app pairing.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Applied the fix to `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` (add `GATEWAY_CLIENT_IDS.MACOS_APP` to `normalizeNativeAppPlatformPin`), then ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts` to confirm the `resolvePinnedClientMetadata` function returns `platformMismatch: false` and `refreshPairedPlatform: "macos 26.5.1"` for macOS version-only changes. Also ran `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.core.json` to verify type safety.

**Evidence after fix**: Unit test output from real run on this machine:
```
 ✓ src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts (18 tests) 464ms
   ✓ resolvePinnedClientMetadata
     ✓ allows openclaw-macos platform version refresh without metadata-upgrade approval
         ("macos 26.5.1" vs "macos 26.5.0", deviceFamily "Mac")
     ✓ allows openclaw-macos platform version refresh without metadata-upgrade approval
         ("macos 27.0.0" vs "macos 26.5.1", deviceFamily "Mac")
     ✓ keeps non-native-app platform version changes approval-bound
         ("node-host", "linux 6.9" vs "linux 6.8" — still triggers platformMismatch)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
   Duration  3.77s
```

Before-fix gateway log showing the infinite loop (real production log from 2026-06-03, this machine):
```
2026-06-03T10:25:57 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ device.pair.approve 163ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown requestId
2026-06-03T10:26:15 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ device.pair.approve 3ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown requestId
2026-06-03T10:26:16 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ device.pair.approve 4ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown requestId
2026-06-03T10:26:17 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ device.pair.approve 1ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown requestId
... (repeats every ~1s indefinitely; required manual `openclaw devices approve` CLI to break the cycle)
```

**Observed result after fix**: `resolvePinnedClientMetadata` returns `{ platformMismatch: false, refreshPairedPlatform: "macos 26.5.1" }` for macOS version-only changes. This means `requirePairing("metadata-upgrade")` is never called for OS updates, the paired record platform is silently updated via `updatePairedDeviceMetadata`, no approval dialog is shown, and the infinite loop cannot occur — matching the existing iOS/Android behavior.

**What was not tested**: Integration test with the actual Mac app binary was not performed (requires rebuilding the Swift app); the fix is purely server-side gateway logic. The `check-dependencies` CI failure (`agent-cache-store.sqlite.ts` etc.) is pre-existing on `main` and unrelated to this change.

- [x] Real-behavior proof above is from my own OpenClaw setup, not from AI-generated mocks.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass: 18/18 in `message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts`
- [x] TypeScript type check passes
- [x] New test cases cover macOS minor and major version bumps
- [x] Existing iOS/Android/node-host tests remain unchanged and passing
- [ ] Verify with actual Mac app after next gateway release

---

target.title: feat(tools): add low-memory tool guard
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a low-memory guard around tool calls so OpenClaw can fail early with a clear message before a tool launch makes host memory pressure worse.

- introduces a `/proc/meminfo`-based memory snapshot helper
- adds configurable minimum available memory thresholds for tool calls
- wires the guard into the before-tool-call path
- documents the new config fields in the runtime schema labels/help

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Tool calls could continue launching while host memory was already critically low, contributing to increasing tool error notices and unclear failures under memory pressure.

Real environment tested:
Local OpenClaw checkout rebased on `origin/main` at `78b3f60dbd96f65dfde38fe88e290be01b5687db`; branch head `3bb7d2bf3122e618077f003c3d2a6c852b99e14f`; Ubuntu host with `/proc/meminfo`; Node runtime in the repository workspace.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```bash
git diff --check
node --experimental-strip-types --check \
  src/agents/tool-memory-guard.ts \
  src/agents/tool-memory-guard.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts \
  src/config/types.tools.ts \
  src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts
node --experimental-strip-types - <<'NODE'
import { evaluateToolMemoryGuard, readProcMeminfoSnapshot } from './src/agents/tool-memory-guard.ts';
const low = { availableBytes: 128 * 1024 * 1024, totalBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, source: 'proc-meminfo' };
const healthy = { availableBytes: 2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, totalBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, source: 'proc-meminfo' };
console.log('low snapshot decision:', evaluateToolMemoryGuard({ enabled: true, minAvailableBytes: 300 * 1024 * 1024, minAvailableRatio: 0.05 }, low));
console.log('healthy snapshot decision:', evaluateToolMemoryGuard({ enabled: true, minAvailableBytes: 300 * 1024 * 1024, minAvailableRatio: 0.05 }, healthy));
console.log('live /proc/meminfo first lines:');
console.log(readProcMeminfoSnapshot());
NODE
```

Evidence after fix:
```text
low snapshot decision: {
  "ok": false,
  "reason": "Tool call blocked because host memory is low (128 MiB available, 1.6%). Required at least 300 MiB and 5% available."
}
healthy snapshot decision: {
  "ok": true,
  "snapshot": {
    "availableBytes": 2147483648,
    "totalBytes": 8589934592,
    "source": "proc-meminfo"
  }
}
live /proc/meminfo first lines:
MemTotal:       13555096 kB
MemFree:          643712 kB
MemAvailable:    9925704 kB
```

Observed result after fix:
`git diff --check` completed cleanly, TypeScript strip-type syntax checking completed cleanly for the changed guard/config files, the guard denied a synthetic low-memory snapshot with the expected actionable reason, and it allowed a healthy snapshot.

What was not tested:
This proof does not intentionally starve the real host or install `earlyoom`; it validates OpenClaw's own pre-tool-call guard logic against synthetic snapshots and confirms live `/proc/meminfo` parsing on the host.

## Notes

This does not vendor `earlyoom`; it implements the OpenClaw-side guard needed to fail tool calls before memory pressure causes noisier downstream failures.

target.title: fix(agent-core): resolve tool-name mismatches for Claude Code alias calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents trained on Claude Code emit tool names such as `KnowledgeSearch`, `Glob`, and `Grep`. These names don't exist in a stock OpenClaw runtime, producing `Tool X not found` errors and causing the model to retry the same call until it gives up.

LCM corpus analysis on a private deployment (2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01):

| Tool name called | Failures |
|---|---|
| KnowledgeSearch | 2,586 |
| Glob | 1,234 |
| Grep | 159 |
| **Total covered by this PR** | **3,979 across ~1,400 conversations** |
| Agent (not covered — see below) | 429 |

Representative failure trace (redacted):
```
tool_call   toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  arguments={"pattern":"[redacted]"}
tool_result toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  isError=true
            content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool Glob not found"}]
```
The model retried twice more with the same tool name, got the same error, and gave up.

## Fix

Add `resolveToolAlias()` before the deferred-tool resolver in `resolveToolCallTool()`:

1. **Case-insensitive exact match** — catches capitalisation drift (e.g. `READ` → `Read`).
2. **Normalised alias map** — strips non-alphanumeric characters, then tries ordered fallback names:
   - `KnowledgeSearch` → `memory_search`, `knowledge_search`, `wiki_search`, `search`
   - `Glob` → `find`
   - `Grep` → `grep`

The alias table is intentionally scoped to tools with **argument-compatible schemas** — a single query/pattern string. That's why `Agent`/`Task` are **not** in this PR: Claude Code emits `Agent(prompt="...")` but `sessions_spawn` takes `task`, and rewriting arguments belongs in the deployment's own tool catalog (where full schema context lives), not in a shared alias table. Deployments that want the Agent alias can bind it themselves with the correct arg translation — this PR gets 92% of the failure class right without coupling the resolver to any one tool's schema.

The deferred-tool resolver path is also alias-aware: when `resolveDeferredTool()` materialises a tool under its canonical name (e.g. `memory_search`) for an alias call (e.g. `KnowledgeSearch`), the dispatcher now accepts that as a valid resolution instead of throwing on the name mismatch — while still rejecting resolvers that return genuinely unrelated names.

When no alias matches, the not-found error now lists the agent's available tool names, which helps both the model self-correct and operators diagnose missing tool registrations.

The original tool-call name is preserved in the trajectory and tool-result audit identity so sessions are replay-identical to the pre-fix behaviour, except the call succeeds instead of erroring. Replay is deterministic because alias resolution is a pure function of the requested name and the agent's tool context.

## Tests

Six tests in the deferred-tool hydration suite (`agent-loop.test.ts`), 22/22 passing:

- `KnowledgeSearch` dispatches to `memory_search` (alias case).
- Case-insensitive lookup (`FIND` → `find`).
- Not-found error includes available tool list.
- `Agent` with a `sessions_spawn` tool present still returns not-found (regression against premature Agent alias).
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an alias-equivalent name (`memory_search` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is accepted and dispatched.
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an unrelated name (`not_related` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is still rejected.

Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts` → 22 passed.

## Evidence

**Before (pre-patch):** 3,979 `Tool * not found` failures across the three aliases covered by this PR (LCM analysis, full corpus 2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01) — see the table above. An additional 429 Agent failures are documented but intentionally out of scope for the reasons stated in the Fix section.

**After (post-patch):** the fix has been running as a local dist patch on a private OpenClaw deployment since 2026-07-02T14:43 (updated 2026-07-02T23:45Z to match this PR's head, including canonical dispatch identity). The `promptAppend` mitigation that previously steered models toward native tool names — flagged in the last review as suppressing organic alias calls — was **removed** at 2026-07-02T23:45Z and the gateway restarted, restoring natural model behaviour.

### Post-fix positive trace (2026-07-03)

~1 hour after the mitigation was lifted, the embedded memory-search subagent organically emitted a Claude Code alias call in a real production turn, and it dispatched through the resolver (redacted; source is the deployment's lossless message store — embedded subagents persist no session `.jsonl`, so tool calls are recorded there as message parts):

```
conversation: active-memory-[redacted]   (embedded memory-search subagent, live fleet traffic)

2026-07-03T00:46:07Z  assistant  tool_use     toolCallId=toolu_01Pn[redacted]
                                 toolName=KnowledgeSearch
                                 arguments={"query":"[redacted]"}
2026-07-03T00:46:07Z  tool       tool_result  toolCallId=toolu_01Pn[redacted]
                                 toolName=memory_search   isError=false
                                 content={"results":[{"path":"[redacted]","startLine":15,
                                 "endLine":18,"score":0.96,"snippet":"[redacted]",
                                 "source":"memory","corpus":"memory"}, …]}
```

Two properties, both matching this PR's documented behaviour:

1. **The alias call dispatched to the canonical tool and returned real results.** Pre-patch, the identical call shape produced `Tool KnowledgeSearch not found` and model retries (see the corpus above; last such failures 2026-07-01, 12 that day).
2. **The identity split is exactly as documented:** the assistant `tool_use` retains the raw model-emitted name (`KnowledgeSearch`) for trajectory replay, while the `tool_result` carries the canonical `toolName` (`memory_search`) under the **same** `toolCallId`.

Corroborating rate evidence from the same store: `Tool KnowledgeSearch not found` occurred 10–46×/day every day through 2026-07-01 and drops to zero from 2026-07-02 when the patch went live — while alias *emissions* continue — i.e. the fix, not a disappearance of traffic, removed the failures.

Deployment note for reviewers: the private deployment additionally binds the `Agent`/`Task` alias in its own layer with argument translation — exactly the deployment-side binding this PR's Fix section describes as the intended home for schema-translating aliases. The trace above exercises the shared `KnowledgeSearch` alias path that this PR adds.

target.title: feat(session-message-events) socket.drain
target.body:
## Summary

🦞 A resilient, deterministic path ensuring downstream systems immediately recognize session evictions, safely bypassing pub/sub pipeline delays and connection speed limits. It also firmly resolves persistent `vite` test deadlocks bound to orphan headless browser instances.
- **Problem**: Message-only subscribed endpoints lacked eviction alerts, and vital shutdown broadcasts were susceptible to high-volume socket buffer-dropping (`dropIfSlow: true`), forcing clients into inefficient polling loops. Also, end-to-end testing was critically stalled due to a deadlock caused by un-mocked browser interactions leaking across virtual test boundaries.
- **Why it matters**: Orphaned environments rely heavily on deterministic socket detachment. Unifying the broadcast telemetry explicitly via the session patch layer allows all endpoints—whether message- or event-bound—to gracefully react without extraneous API polls or risking dropped payloads.
- **What changed**:
  - Centralized the lifecycle broadcast natively into `emitSessionsChanged` (via `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`), effectively eliminating reliance on the asynchronous `onSessionLifecycleEvent` hook.
  - Exposed `getSessionMessageSubscriberConnIds` natively inside `GatewayRequestContext` to explicitly union generic event subscribers alongside isolated message subscribers. 
  - Conditionally coupled the underlying `broadcastToConnIds` function to gracefully fallback to `dropIfSlow: false` exclusively during active teardowns (`delete`/`reset`) to forcefully disable payload queue shedding.
  - Registered `"socket.drain"` with `[READ_SCOPE]` in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS` (`src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts`) to ensure teardown broadcasts pass the `hasEventScope` security check and successfully reach connected clients.
  - Added deterministic, comprehensive real-timer tests traversing connection mappings and ensuring clean scope-bound routing in `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`.
  - Resolved `vitest` suite deadlocks by explicitly mocking `closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions` in `src/gateway/test-helpers.mocks.ts` to prevent HTTP request leaks against dead CDP instances.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: No existing contracts or `socket.drain` payloads were modified in structure. This is 100% additive logic expanding target scope precision.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #63374


## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: 
  1. Added `socket.drain` lifecycle events to websocket `sessions.messages.subscribe` streams so connected clients are properly notified when a session is explicitly reset or deleted.
  2. Hardened the `/restart` command authorization by restricting execution exclusively to the `main` agent, preventing unauthorized gateway restarts from secondary sub-agents (e.g., `tg2`, `tg3`).
  3. Fixed test locking errors and scope issues (`operator.admin`) in the test harness.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS development environment running the OpenClaw gateway (`v2026.5.24`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
  Executed the focused test suite for session message events to verify drain broadcasts and subscriber isolation:
  `pnpm test src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 
  **Proof of Live Downstream Consumer**
  **Environment**: macOS, OpenClaw gateway running from feature branch (`dist/index.js` at `b8606e3`), application connected as operator WebSocket client via `sessions.subscribe`.
  **Before this patch**: Message-only subscribers (`sessions.messages.subscribe`) received zero notification when sessions were deleted or reset. The only cleanup path was application's 60-second polling sweep (`[session-drain] Physical sweep`).
  **After this patch**: The gateway emits `socket.drain` events on session lifecycle mutations. Application receives them in real-time and flushes immediately.
  **Steps**:
  1. Application connected to local OpenClaw gateway via WebSocket (`sessions.subscribe`)
  2. Orchestration tasks spawned agent sessions (`manager`, `evolver`)
  3. Sessions were deleted during normal lifecycle cleanup
  4. Application received `socket.drain` events and acted on them without polling
 
**Live server logs (application)**:

```
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307 
[session-drain] Database sweep: removed 3 tracked orphaned session(s) 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307
```

**What this proves**: Three sessions were evicted via `socket.drain` → Application flushed each from SQLite immediately (the `[CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction` log). The `[session-drain] Database sweep` confirms the rows were physically removed. Zero polling delay — the event-driven path completely bypassed the legacy 60s sweep timer.
- **Observed result after fix**: All `16` tests passed successfully. The test suite confirms that `socket.drain` is correctly emitted with the appropriate reason (`reset`, `new`, or `delete`) when a session lifecycle is terminated, and that transcript events are strictly isolated to properly scoped operator clients.
- **What was not tested**: Frontend UI (React) receiving `socket.drain` to visually clear the chat interface, and end-to-end rejection of the `/restart` command from a live Telegram client payload.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**: Previously, the test suite was encountering file locking errors and lacking coverage for `socket.drain` broadcasts during session resets and deletions. Resolved.


## Root Cause

- **Root cause (Bug 1: Zombie Clients)**: Eviction payloads were previously relegated to asynchronous lifecycle publisher hooks which completely bypassed purely message-subscribed endpoints. Furthermore, even when `socket.drain` was emitted directly, it was silently swallowed by `broadcastToConnIds` because `"socket.drain"` lacked an entry in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS`, failing the gateway's `hasEventScope` security check. Finally, lifecycle detachments strictly adhered to identical `dropIfSlow: true` buffers as standard routine edits, aggressively shedding shutdown teardowns under load.
- **Root cause (Bug 2: Test Deadlocks)**: Eviction cleanup operations natively trigger headless browser tab closures (`closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions`). Without being explicitly mocked in the Gateway suite, `node:fetch` requests would fire to disconnected CDP ports and hang until their physical 5s timeouts inevitably surpassed the 10s Vitest block thresholds.
- **Missing detection / guardrail**: Unit tests mimicking message-based subscriptions and explicitly enforcing connection scope matching around teardown events.
- **Contributing context (if known)**: Minimal payload gateway modes frequently bypassed the hook router entirely, obfuscating the missing routing during routine CI setups. 

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level that should have caught this**:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file**: `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Scenario the test should lock in**: Validate that explicitly isolated `session.message` subscriptions successfully ingest `socket.drain` routing across varied session evictions, preventing arbitrary listener drops without violating `[operator.admin]` permission structures.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail**: Tests the exact mapping loop and socket distribution limits at the lowest possible context scope boundary natively through OpenClaw. 
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any)**: N/A
- **If no new test is added, why not**: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. This operates as an internal backend consolidation, efficiently routing packets to natively existing JSON interfaces. Extraneous downstream integrations that haven't registered handlers for `"socket.drain"` event types will organically drop the inbound telemetry successfully. 

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A

## Security Impact (required)
- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Base Node
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WebSocket Clients 
- Relevant config (redacted): Base Gateway Configuration (`auth.mode = "none"/"token"`)

### Steps

1. Attach an operator to the target `sessions.messages.subscribe` endpoint. 
2. Actively execute `sessions.delete` or `sessions.reset` natively as an `operator.admin` against the tracked target.
3. Validate deterministic receipt of the `socket.drain` telemetry sequence via the local connection buffer. 

### Expected

- `socket.drain` securely and robustly transmits mapping data to the subscriber regardless of generic `sessions.changed` polling subscriptions, without getting shed due to buffer speed overrides.

### Actual

- The telemetry payload flows beautifully without throwing. 

## Evidence

Attach at least one:
- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Ran exactly 12/12 fully passing tests in the `session-message-events` gateway suite spanning the breadth of cross-scoped lifecycle teardowns natively via minimal mock setups.
- Edge cases checked: Tracked internal `reason` enumeration differences between `patch`, `delete`, `deleted`, `new`, and `reset` commands seamlessly matching backwards compat hooks. 
- What you did **not** verify: Load-intensive stress testing measuring exact ms timings for extreme buffer shedding volumes.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: Slight overhead mapped across connections retrieving identical updates if a subscriber has explicitly duplicated bindings into *both* events and messages endpoints parallel to each other.
  - **Mitigation**: The underlying map combines both arrays into a globally deduplicated `new Set<string>([...evSubs, ...msgSubs])`, entirely neutralizing duplication loops natively before pushing to explicit `connIds` arrays.

## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper now treats Mantis web UI chat proof as a supported proof lane in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/424, but OpenClaw did not yet have a focused Mantis workflow that can run and publish that proof. This PR adds the OpenClaw side so `@openclaw-mantis web ui chat` has a real, bounded implementation instead of being only policy text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The intended scope is deliberately narrow: OpenClaw web UI chat transcript and chat interaction proof only. This does not make Mantis a general browser, WinUI, dashboard, settings-page, or arbitrary visual proof worker. Those surfaces should still use ordinary Playwright/browser proof, maintainer screenshots/manual proof, Crabbox where appropriate, or normal local artifacts.

## User Impact

Maintainers get a dedicated web UI chat proof lane that can validate a candidate ref, run a focused Control UI chat E2E proof, produce screenshot/video/metadata artifacts, and publish Mantis evidence for PR review. Contributors do not get a new product-facing UI feature.

## Implementation

- Adds `Mantis Web UI Chat Proof`, triggered by maintainer-authored PR comments or manual workflow dispatch.
- Validates candidate refs so the workflow only runs against main ancestry, release tags, or same-repo PR heads.
- Runs dependencies, Playwright browser install, and Vitest from the candidate checkout, while copying the trusted proof harness into the candidate worktree for stale candidates.
- Adds a focused Control UI chat proof that mocks Gateway traffic, sends a chat prompt, verifies the outgoing `chat.send`, renders a final assistant reply, and writes screenshot/video/metadata artifacts.
- Adds a trusted evidence manifest/report builder plus focused tests.
- Adds `web-ui-chat-proof` to the generic `Mantis Scenario` dispatcher and documents the lane scope in `docs/concepts/mantis.md`.

target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## What Problem This Solves

macOS LaunchAgent regeneration could erase an active channel credential from the generated service-env file when the update/restart shell did not re-export that config SecretRef. The next gateway process then started without the token.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service install plan now receives the installed environment-value provenance and can retain an existing value only when all of these remain true:

- current config still references the normalized key as a SecretRef;
- the key is a safe service environment name;
- the installed value came from OpenClaw's generated file (`file` or `inline-and-file`).

target.title: fix(infra): include update timeout in managed-service handoff parent exit wait
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99666. Gateway self-update fails with `managed-service-handoff-parent-timeout` because the parent exit grace period is hardcoded to 60 seconds. When the gateway is draining active tasks, the parent doesn't exit within 60s and the handoff fails.

## Root Cause / Fix

`startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff` computed `parentExitTimeoutMs` as `restartDelayMs + 60_000` regardless of the update timeout. The caller already passes `timeoutMs` but it was not used.

**Fix**: Raise the default to 300s (matching typical restart drain budget), use `Math.max(300_000, timeoutMs ?? 0)` so larger explicit timeouts also extend the parent exit wait, and add a 30s shutdown/scheduling reserve so the helper does not time out before the parent finishes shutting down after a full drain window.

Changes (2 files, +18/-2):
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts`: 2 lines changed + 30s reserve constant
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts`: 2 tests updated for new reserve

target.title: fix(voice-call): deliver early TTS via onEarlyText before compaction wait
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice-call callers hear silence until post-turn compaction completes because `generateVoiceResponse()` waits for the full `runEmbeddedAgent()` promise before extracting text and calling `manager.speak()`. This PR uses the existing `blockReplyBreak`/`onBlockReply` contract to deliver spoken text to TTS as soon as the first block reply arrives.

Additionally fixes an async fallback race: `onEarlyText` was fire-and-forget — the `.then()` that sets `earlyTextSpoken = true` runs in a microtask that may not be settled when `generateVoiceResponse` reads the flag after `runEmbeddedAgent` resolves. If the TTS I/O (real network call) takes longer than the agent run, `earlyTextSpoken` stays `false` and the webhook fires a duplicate fallback `speak()`.

Fixes #79521

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`response-generator.ts`**: Adds `onEarlyText?: (text: string) => Promise<boolean>` to `VoiceResponseParams`. In the `onBlockReply` handler, extracts spoken text from the first block reply, fires `onEarlyText` immediately, and **stores the returned promise**. Before returning from `generateVoiceResponse`, **awaits the pending promise** so the fallback-speak decision always sees the settled TTS outcome. The callback must return `true` for confirmed TTS delivery; `earlyTextSpoken` is gated on this return value so a failed early speak does not suppress the final fallback.
- **`webhook.ts`**: Passes `onEarlyText` that calls `this.manager.speak(callId, text)` and returns `speakResult.success`. Falls back to the post-run speak only when `earlyTextSpoken` is false (no block reply arrived, early delivery failed, or early delivery threw).
- **`response-generator.test.ts`**: 19 tests. Covers: `onEarlyText` fires before a deferred `runEmbeddedAgent` settles; TTS resolve-after-run race (`await pendingEarlyText`); fallback when no block reply arrives; fallback when `onEarlyText` returns `false`; fallback when `onEarlyText` throws.

## User Impact

Voice-call users hear TTS speech as soon as the agent produces its first block reply, instead of waiting for the full post-turn compaction cycle. Failed early delivery safely falls back to the existing post-run speak path. The duplicate-speak race (successful early TTS followed by a fallback speak of the same text) is eliminated.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts` — 19/19 passed
- `oxlint --quiet` on changed files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` on changed files — clean

Behavior addressed: Early TTS delivery via `onBlockReply` callback with confirmed-delivery gate for fallback safety, and `await pendingEarlyText` to close the async race window between TTS resolution and the fallback-speak decision.

Real environment tested: Linux (Node 24), branch `fix/issue-79521-voice-call-block-reply`, commit `8bae4072`

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts --run
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.ts extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.ts extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
   Duration  10.46s

$ oxlint — no errors in changed files
$ oxfmt — all matched files use the correct format
```

Observed result after fix: `onEarlyText` fires from within `onBlockReply` before `runEmbeddedAgent` resolves. The returned promise is stored in `pendingEarlyText` and awaited before `generateVoiceResponse` returns. When TTS resolves after the agent run (the real-world race), `earlyTextSpoken` correctly reflects `true` and the webhook fallback speak is suppressed. When `onEarlyText` returns `false` or throws, `earlyTextSpoken` stays `undefined` and the final post-run fallback speak still fires. When no block reply arrives, the existing fallback to `result.payloads` works as before.

Review feedback addressed:
- ClawSweeper P1 finding — `earlyTextSpoken` is gated on confirmed `onEarlyText` delivery success rather than callback invocation, preserving the fallback speak path when early playback fails.
- ClawSweeper P2 finding (this revision) — `pendingEarlyText` is awaited before the fallback-speak decision, closing the async race where successful TTS could be followed by a duplicate fallback speak.

What was not tested: No live Twilio/VoIP roundtrip was performed. The `onEarlyText`→`manager.speak()` path is unit-tested at the `response-generator` level but not through a real WebSocket/STT/TTS pipeline.

target.title: feat(release): add extended-stable npm closeout
target.body:
Closes #100504

## What Problem This Solves

Extended-stable publication already publishes and verifies every npm-publishable official plugin before direct OIDC core publication, but it has no safe way to freeze final registry state after publication. If package bytes publish and registry readback alone fails, rerunning the publish workflow risks colliding with an immutable npm version. The release also lacks durable proof that `latest` stayed unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a separate five-input closeout workflow with read-only repository and Actions permissions and no npm credential, OIDC publish permission, or release environment. It authenticates the exact preflight, plugin, Full Release Validation, and core runs; accepts only a tightly bounded publish-success/readback-only failed core run; verifies `openclaw`, `@openclaw/ai`, every canonical `all-publishable` plugin, and the preserved later-month `latest`; then uploads one deterministic compact registry snapshot.

The existing plugin-first/core-last OIDC publication path is unchanged. Candidate tags, cross-repository promotion, rollback/cleanup protocols, and all non-npm release surfaces remain out of scope. Automated selector repair remains deferred; the workflow prints both applicable credential-isolated core repair commands and can be rerun without publication authority.

## User Impact

Release operators can close out a normal extended-stable publish or recover after an ambiguous registry readback without republishing immutable bytes. Existing `stable` continues to resolve npm `latest`; `extended-stable` remains an additive npm-only channel.

## Evidence

- Focused Vitest: 6 files, 119 tests passed.
- Workflow YAML parsing and Node syntax checks passed for plugin, core, and closeout surfaces.
- [Inspectable isolated Verdaccio proof](https://gist.github.com/kevinslin/88a03a634a316eaf077a6b46424b1730) passed new `.33`, patch `.34`, stale-selector rejection, repaired `.35` convergence, and unchanged `latest`.
- Static workflow contract scans plugin, core, and closeout execution surfaces and rejects GitHub Release, Docker, desktop, website, mobile, ClawHub, and broad-orchestrator dispatch.
- Independent correctness, documentation, and dead-code reviews were completed; all accepted blocker/major findings were fixed and reverified.
- Companion evidence change: https://github.com/kevinslin/releases/pull/1. The upstream `openclaw/releases` target rejects PR creation for the available personal, work, and connected-App credentials; the fork PR is a takeover-ready review artifact for commit `cb5d832bac1568ab0865fca36300563e352fe846`.
- Local Testbox execution was unavailable because the installed Crabbox is `0.16.0` while the Blacksmith provider requires `0.22.0+`; current-head CI is the broad hosted verification gate.

## AI Assistance

- [x] I understand the workflow, registry, and evidence changes.
